output.summary: The initial request from SH-SUP (CL-01) was to build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for refund-status answers. Investigation instead found the root problem (PD-1) is a payment-process data-quality defect: refunds fail at submission due to invalid IBAN data (E-01: 5/5 sampled payment-db.refund_failures records show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT), which generates repeat support tickets - not a missing self-service channel or slow agent response (E-02: 2.0h median response vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets). The release delivers the completed root-cause investigation for both DA-PAY and DA-TCK (work items DONE), reached under a DEFINE Gate CONDITIONAL_PASS. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds) because the actual fix actions (IBAN validation/correction) are blocked by an open verification obligation about whether the 5-record sample represents the full failure population; only the diagnostic finding is in scope for release, not the remediation.
key_points: PD-1 root_problem: refunds fail at the payment-processing step due to invalid IBAN data (E-01: 5/5 sampled refund_failures = FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT), causing repeat status tickets - this contradicts the original chatbot framing (CL-01, CL-02).
E-02 shows ticket median response time is 2.0h against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, ruling out slow agent response as the driver of the symptom.
Hypothesis H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE is SUPPORTED by E-01; H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL, H-INFORMATION-VISIBILITY-GAP, H-PROCESS-HANDOFF-FRICTION and H-TICKET-VOLUME-OVERLOAD are REJECTED.

DEFINE Gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring unknown U-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS to VOB-U-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS, which blocks the validate_iban_format and correct_invalid_iban_records actions on DA-PAY.

Released scope is the investigate_refund_failure_root_cause work on DA-PAY and DA-TCK (W-WI-DA-PAY-INVESTIGATION, W-WI-DA-TCK-INVESTIGATION, both DONE) - a diagnostic deliverable, matching solution_design.release_scope.

The proposed remediations (SR-IBAN-VALIDATION-AT-SUBMISSIO, SR-CORRECT-EXISTING-IBAN-RECORD) are not released; they remain pending resolution of the open VOB and lack of evidenced replacement IBAN data.
The link between repeat tickets and IBAN failures (A-TICKETS-DRIVEN-BY-FAILURES) is an active assumption, not confirmed by ticket content (U-TICKET-CONTENT-LINKAGE remains OPEN).
Conflicts C-1, C-2 and C-3 over refund_wait.root_cause remain OPEN, reflecting unresolved tension between stakeholder framing (CL-01, CL-02, E-03) and the tool evidence (E-01, E-02).
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass - deferred items are tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before this release.

VOB-U-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS is still OPEN: whether the 5-record sample (E-01) represents the full refund-failure population is unverified, and this blocks validate_iban_format and correct_invalid_iban_records on DA-PAY, both outside this release's scope.

Ticket response speed (E-02: 2.0h median vs 24h SLA, 900 tickets) is already well within SLA, which confirms response speed is not the problem that needs solving - it is a boundary finding, not a fix.

This investigation (E-01) diagnoses the IBAN failure pattern but does not itself fix any failed refund; the proposed sample-verification step (SR-RESOLVE-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIV) is a check, not a remediation.
DA-PAY completeness is recorded as UNKNOWN until a full-population query is run, so the representativeness of the 5-record sample cannot yet be confirmed.

Even once representativeness is confirmed, correcting existing FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records (SR-CORRECT-EXISTING-IBAN-RECORD) would still require accurate replacement IBAN data that is not currently evidenced.
